summary: ADR 0020 §3. TYPE_ROLES has carried a weight, leading and tracking per role since ADR 0009, and only the size ever reached a page; components chose the rest per call site, and about 49 of 137 role usages disagreed with the table on weight alone. The maintainer decided on 2026-09-24 that the TABLE is the source of truth. Each role now has three brandable tokens (`--ui-text-<role>-weight|-leading|-tracking`, 39 in all), and the Tailwind emitter hangs them on the size utility as v4 companions, so `text-body-md` sets size, weight, line-height and letter-spacing from one class. An explicit font-/leading-/tracking- still wins, because Tailwind reads each companion through --tw-*. The weight ladder and trackings moved from fixed to brandable, with two new knobs: `typography.weights` re-points a ladder step onto the cuts a brand face really has, and every role on that step follows; `typography.tracking: "font"` zeroes every tracking. Leading has no knob. 242 per-call-site weight/leading/tracking classes were removed across 47 files; roles that disagreed with the table now render the table (examples: label-md and caption go 500→600; body-lg titles in Drawer, Toast, ImageOverlay and Accordion's body-sm trigger go 600→500; Textarea's value goes 500→400). This is a deliberate VISUAL change. Nine declared exceptions keep designed differences that following the table would erase, each by part and attribute with a reason: resting Calendar days and month/year options one weight step under button-sm, so the selected one reads heavier; the Sidebar section label heavier than its items; the Sidebar profile name heavier than its email; the ChatMessage sender at 1.35 against the receiver's 1.55; and Textarea and Sidebar rows on their sheet leading, so the 128px box and the 46px row keep their heights. Badge dropped its vertical padding so its pinned 22/28px heights absorb label-sm's 1.3 leading. Enforced at RUNTIME, because a component's size map and base classes are separate strings that cn() joins only in the browser: a Storybook afterEach fails any story where an element naming text-<role> renders another weight, leading or tracking than its role, unless its data-slot is a declared exception. It failed 152 of 237 stories before the migration and passes all 237 after. `check:type-roles` fails on an exception naming a part that no longer exists (probed).

migration.manual: Regenerate your token CSS before syncing components from this revision: the synced components no longer set weight/leading/tracking themselves and rely on the role companions, so against an older theme they would fall back to inherited values. In your own code, drop font-/leading-/tracking- classes that sit beside a text-<role> unless you mean to deviate from the role.
